spacing.note: em multiples of a 0.96vw base (13.824px at 1440); gutter --pad = max(18px, 2.2vw); section padding 6.2em

colors.role: accent: alternate headings, current link, flags, hairlines, checked controls
shade behind normal-size lime text (nav strip)
veil over photo areas without text

taste.name: The photograph is the only light in the room
taste.trigger: When the site needed to feel brighter and warmer without breaking the forest identity
taste.decision: Kept every section on forest and let bright daylight photos carry the lightness, over introducing a cream or white section background
taste.reason: A single dark ground makes each photo read like a window onto the pasture; a light section would compete with the photos and turn them back into rectangles on a page
evidence: forest is 77.6% / 79.1% / 99.5% of background area on Home / Beef / Contact
no gray or cream value anywhere
replaced heroes are sunlit pasture (Home, Invest) and a sunlit corral (Beef)

taste.name: Darkness only where the words are
taste.trigger: When bright skies sat behind white titles and caps labels
taste.decision: Pooled forest behind each block of text and left the rest of the photo almost bare, over darkening the whole photo evenly
taste.reason: Readers need contrast exactly under the letters and nowhere else; an even overlay buys legibility by dimming the very photo meant to lift the mood
evidence: lowest measured text contrast 4.76:1 over a pure white photo
Contact hero shows clear pasture between the title pool and the side-text pool

taste.name: No boxes, no depth
taste.trigger: When grouping buttons, form fields, cards and FAQs
taste.decision: Built every component from 1.5px hairlines on a flat surface, over rounded cards with shadows
taste.reason: A ranch and its paperwork feel closer to a printed field ledger than to an app; flat lines keep attention on the content and the photos instead of on component chrome
evidence: form inputs are hairline boxes with a square lime check

taste.name: Big signposts, small print
taste.trigger: When ordering headings, labels and body text
taste.decision: Jumped from 37-64px uppercase titles straight to 11-18px text, over a graduated scale with intermediate sizes
taste.reason: Visitors skim a marketing page by its titles; a large gap makes each title an unmistakable stop, and everything under it reads as the detail you choose to read
evidence: weights 400 and 700 only; 700 reserved for Orbolo Title
